history.gap: The unscrolled nav reserves width for the later "— OPEN DE DISCORD ↗" swap, so at rest DISCORD sits in an ~85px hole on either side while every other item is spaced ~28px; it reads as a broken flex gap, not a feature. At the bar the item keeps a single measured slot and the scrolled label grows from the dash without disturbing its neighbours (or the whole nav re-centres in one eased move). Beyond that, gold-small-caps-on-black-grain is a well-worn "private capital" costume; the header needs one element that is unmistakably this brand, not the category.
history.motion: No contact sheet supplied; between states the bar compacts, gains a gold hairline and swaps DISCORD for a dashed "OPEN DE DISCORD" — considered choreography, restrained, but the static reservation for it is visible.
history.verdict: B has the more distinctive atmosphere and a genuinely good vertical logotype, but it ships a struck-through mobile nav, low-contrast labels and no scrolled behaviour, which no jury forgives. A is the more generic idiom yet is built with real care — language switcher underline, scrolled hairline and label swap, tidy mobile — and loses points only for the gapped Discord slot and a look that belongs to the category rather than the brand.

history.gap: The header is competent but reads as the stock "dark + gold hairline + tracked serif caps" fintech idiom, and the details that should sell it are loose: the centred nav group sits ~16px right of the page axis, a stray mid-dot separator floats between KANALEN and DISCORD with no partner elsewhere, and on scroll the label morphs into "OPEN DE  DISCORD" with a visibly doubled word-space and the gold dash colliding into the label. At the bar, the nav is either truly centred or honestly left-set on the same 64px margin as the logo and eyebrow, separators are a system (all or none), and the scroll-state CTA is a single tracked string with the gold rule set at a fixed optical gap.
history.motion: Header compacts on scroll into a slim bar with a bottom hairline and the Discord item reveals a gold dash + CTA label; a considered choreography, though the label spacing snaps rather than settles.
history.verdict: A is a disciplined but familiar dark-luxury header whose small alignment and spacing slips keep it off the shortlist; B has the more distinctive mark and atmosphere but ships an illegible, arbitrarily placed desktop nav and a visibly broken mobile nav. Craft beats mood here: A wins on clarity, detail and a real scrolled state, with neither site at Site-of-the-Day standard as-is.
